note: Second state off the federal gap list. 39 RIDB rows, 13 of them likely_rv by catalog; all 13 added. Mostly BLM and Forest Service, none with hookups - the western public-land pattern RV Life under-lists.

added.name: Hinman Campground (Elk River)
added.caveat: no published site length or permitted-equipment list; phone recorded per AWH's rule (Hahns Peak/Bears Ears RD, verified off the rec.gov page rather than assumed from neighbouring Seedhouse)

added.name: Oh Be Joyful Campground (Slate River)
added.caveat: BLM 3220 access road is steep and rough, high clearance advised for larger rigs; stated in the note

added.name: Penitente Canyon Campground
added.caveat: short sites - longest stated is 25 ft and only three reach it; stated in the note

added.name: The Bank Campground (Shelf Road)
added.caveat: no published site length or permitted-equipment list; phone recorded per AWH's rule (BLM Royal Gorge Field Office)

added.name: Zapata Falls Campground
added.caveat: RIDB pins this at the CO-150 turnoff on the valley floor; location corrected to the loop itself, ~600 m up the access road, found by reading the imagery

method_notes: 8 of the 13 publish NO per-site coordinates, so the pad-plotting trick that carried Arkansas does not apply to them. It did not matter much here because these are open western sites where the imagery is legible on its own - the opposite of Arkansas's canopy. Where it DID matter is the two calls that had to default down for want of per-site data: Pumphouse and Radium both measure 40-80 m to the Colorado, straddling the on-water bound, with no way to resolve which pads fall inside it.
Hinman is the one genuinely illegible look - snow-covered and deeply shadowed - and with no per-site coordinates either, nothing could confirm riverside sites, so it defaults down.

Zapata Falls is the warning about RIDB pins: it sits at a highway junction 600 m from the campground and was NOT flagged coord_suspect, because that flag only fires when nothing in the database is within ~130 km. Verify every pin by finding the loop in the imagery.
